title: Strobogrammatic Number
summary: Determine if a given string num, representing an integer, is strobogrammatic by checking if it appears the same when rotated 180 degrees.
statement: Determine if a given string num, representing an integer, is strobogrammatic by checking if it appears the same when rotated 180 degrees.
constraints: num contains 1–50 decimal digits and has no leading zero unless it is exactly '0'.
After a 180-degree rotation, 0,1,8 map to themselves and 6/9 exchange. Digits 2,3,4,5,7 are invalid.
hints: Rotation reverses position order as well as changing certain digits.
Compare symmetric characters with a map 0→0,1→1,6→9,8→8,9→6.
Move two pointers inward; reject an unmapped left digit or a mapped value unequal to the right digit.
The middle digit of an odd-length number must be 0, 1, or 8.
editorial: A 180-degree rotation sends the leftmost digit to the rightmost position. Each symmetric pair must therefore match the five-entry rotation map. Two pointers verify all pairs in linear time. The independent oracle constructs the same condition position-by-position from an independently declared mapping.

tests.explanation: Rotating and reversing swaps 6 with 9 and 9 with 6, producing the same string.
Digit 2 has no valid 180-degree rotation, so the number is not strobogrammatic.
